advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update docs/plan-review-gate.md:1583-1584 so the '(c)' cross-reference no longer claims blast-radius escalation is the only way a bug review blocks and no longer attributes 'never-blocking language' to section (b), consistent with the readiness-floor blocks now documented in (b).
evidence: docs/plan-review-gate.md:1582-1584: 'A bug whose persisted `file_impact` declares any non-test path leaves the tier and is reviewed by the FULL, blocking-capable rubric — this is the one way a bug review blocks, and it is why the never-blocking language in (a) and (b) is a statement about the tier, not about bugs.'

docs/plan-review-gate.md:1567-1570 (changed in this diff): 'The light tier is still subject to the deterministic readiness floor: P1 (missing `## Acceptance Criteria`), P10 (verification-presence), and P4's description admission limit remain blocking and short-circuit before any LLM call.'
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py:67-68: `_BUG_TIER_BLOCKING_DET_CRITERIA = {"P1", "P4", "P10"}` confirms in-tier deterministic blocks exist independent of blast-radius escalation.
advisory.finding: docs/plan-review-gate.md section (c) still claims blast-radius escalation is 'the one way a bug review blocks' and cites 'the never-blocking language in (a) and (b)', but the change to section (b) now documents P1/P10/P4 as blocking-and-short-circuiting within the light tier before escalation, so (b) no longer contains never-blocking language and the 'one way a bug review blocks' claim is now inaccurate.
scenarios: A contributor reads (c) to understand when a bug review can block and is told escalation is the only path, contradicting (b)'s newly-documented in-tier P1/P10/P4 blocks.
advisory.suggested_fix: Reword lines 1583-1584 to reflect that a bug review can also block on the deterministic readiness floor (P1/P10/P4) within the light tier, and scope the 'never-blocking' framing to the tier's LLM/advisory findings rather than to sections (a) and (b) as a whole.

blocking.finding: The pre-existing test `test_bug_tier_still_downgrades_non_p4_blocks_to_advisory` encodes the OLD bug-tier contract and was not updated by this diff, so it now contradicts the shipped behavior: it feeds an AC-less bug (which trips P1) and asserts `run_llm is True`, `det_blocking == []`, and P1 surfaced as advisory — but the new `_bug_tier_keeps_blocking` keeps P1 blocking, making run_llm False and det_blocking non-empty. The test will fail (or asserts a forbidden state).
scenarios: Running the unit test suite after this change: this test's assertions no longer match the new contract.
